## 2026-07-01 follow-up: opposite-direction asset lock, segment quarantine, and Codex governance

Latest Telegram evidence showed `USDCAD` delivered as `BUY` and then `SELL` within minutes on different timeframes. Root cause:

- Engine storage cooldown was asset+timeframe scoped, so `USDCAD 1d` and `USDCAD 15m` were treated as different active exposures.
- Delivery locks counted only `sent_ok IS TRUE`, so a fresh in-flight reservation could fail to protect the user before Telegram send confirmation was written.

Changes made:

- Engine now has cycle-level asset cooldown in addition to asset+timeframe cooldown. Only one signal per asset can be stored in a cycle, regardless of direction or timeframe.
- Engine DB cooldown now also loads active assets from the last `ASSET_REPEAT_LOCK_HOURS` hours, defaulting to 12, so different-timeframe same-asset signals are blocked before storage.
- Central delivery reservation treats in-flight rows (`sent_ok=false` and `last_error IS NULL`) as locks. A second same-asset signal cannot slip through while the first send is still being confirmed.
- Delivery dedupe now fails closed when its safety query errors instead of falling back to same-signal-id uniqueness only.
- Free/random and extra-signal selection now exclude assets the user received or reserved inside the asset lock window.
- Segment auto-quarantine is enabled by default. Segments with at least `SEGMENT_QUARANTINE_MIN_TRADES=10` terminal outcomes in the lookback and win rate below `SEGMENT_QUARANTINE_MIN_WIN_RATE=45` or average R below `SEGMENT_QUARANTINE_MIN_AVG_R=0` are blocked.
- `/codex_audit` remains admin/owner-gated and now supports local evidence review plus optional OpenAI aggregate-only review. External review sends only grouped metrics and never sends Telegram IDs, user IDs, signal IDs, MT5 credentials, or raw database rows.
- `scripts/analyze_railway_sql_dump.py` can audit exported Railway SQL dumps for same-user/same-asset duplicates, score saturation, outcome distribution, active-message counts, and redacted MT5 linkage status.

Required/recommended Railway env:

```text
ASSET_REPEAT_LOCK_HOURS=12
DELIVERY_SAME_ASSET_COOLDOWN_HOURS=12
DELIVERY_UNRESOLVED_BLOCK_HOURS=168
DELIVERY_INFLIGHT_RETRY_SECONDS=300
SEGMENT_QUARANTINE_ENABLED=1
SEGMENT_QUARANTINE_LOOKBACK_DAYS=30
SEGMENT_QUARANTINE_MIN_TRADES=10
SEGMENT_QUARANTINE_MIN_WIN_RATE=45
SEGMENT_QUARANTINE_MIN_AVG_R=0
OPENAI_CODEX_REVIEW_ENABLED=1
OPENAI_API_KEY=<set in Railway>
OPENAI_CODEX_REVIEW_MODEL=gpt-4.1-mini
```

Post-deploy evidence to watch:

- Engine logs should show `skipped_cycle_asset_cooldown` or `skipped_db_asset_cooldown` for repeated USDCAD/AAVE/CADJPY-style candidates.
- Delivery logs should show `[dedup] Asset gate hit` before any second same-asset send reaches Telegram.
- `/codex_audit weekly` should report `External aggregate AI: ran` when OpenAI env vars are configured, otherwise `off/failed`.

## 2026-07-01 follow-up: Asset Position Manager and score saturation controls

The next hardening pass moved same-asset protection toward a central position-state model rather than scattered dedupe checks.

Changes made:

- Added `services/asset_position_manager.py` as the shared user/asset state resolver. It normalizes delivered/reserved rows and outcomes into `NONE`, `ACTIVE`, `TP1`, `TP2`, `TP3`, `STOPPED`, `EXPIRED`, and `CANCELLED`.
- `record_signal_delivery(...)` now queries the Asset Position Manager before using legacy fallback checks.
- Telegram pre-send asset locks now query the same Asset Position Manager.
- `_signal_display_score(...)` now prefers `score_calibrated` over raw `score` and caps uncalibrated perfect scores to `SCORE_DISPLAY_MAX=99.5` unless `SCORE_ALLOW_HARD_100=1`.
- Engine storage now writes the resolved capped score back into the signal payload before persistence, reducing future `score=100` accumulation.
- `/codex_audit` governance context now includes score saturation and outcome-integrity metrics so it can flag exact-100 score clusters, duplicate outcome rows, and suspicious absence of TP1/TP2 progress rows.

Additional recommended Railway env:

```text
SCORE_SOFT_CAP_ENABLED=1
SCORE_DISPLAY_MAX=99.5
SCORE_ALLOW_HARD_100=0
OUTCOME_IDEMPOTENCY_ENABLED=1
TELEGRAM_IDEMPOTENCY_ENABLED=1
MT5_IDEMPOTENCY_ENABLED=1
OBSERVABILITY_METRICS_ENABLED=1
EXECUTION_ELIGIBILITY_ENABLED=1
```

## 2026-07-01 follow-up: trader profiles, command reliability, and DB pressure

This follow-up converts SignalRankAI from a single swing-biased signal stream into a profile-aware trading system. The engine now annotates each signal with a trader profile (`scalp`, `day`, `swing`, or `position`), profile-specific expected hold time, expiry, and target model. Telegram users can select a preferred profile with `/profile`; dispatch filters signals to that profile before delivery.

Changes made:

- Added `services/trade_profiles.py` for profile normalization, ATR-based TP/SL shaping, expected time-to-target scoring, user profile persistence, and profile delivery matching.
- Added `services/trading_ledger.py` as the first event-ledger layer for generated signals and guarded state transitions.
- Added `/profile` and owner-only `/db_health` Telegram commands, plus matching command-access/help entries.
- Hardened the Telegram command audit wrapper with command timeouts, error references, and DB-pressure logging so “too many clients” failures become diagnosable instead of silent UX failures.
- Added database pool diagnostics and Postgres activity snapshots for Railway monolith operations.
- Updated signal formatting so premium/VIP users see the signal style and expected hold.
- Updated `/signal all` behavior to direct users to `/signals` instead of looking up a fake reference.
- Fixed long-running owner actions so `/force_market_scan` acknowledges immediately and broadcast/terms blasts no longer report success when zero users received the message.
- Hardened `TierDeliveryManager.get_users_for_signal(...)` so it no longer creates an unmanaged async DB session from synchronous code; callers must pass a sync session or use the managed helper that closes its session.

Additional recommended Railway env:

```text
TRADE_PROFILE_ENGINE_ENABLED=1
TRADING_LEDGER_ENABLED=1
COMMAND_HANDLER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=60
DB_POOL_PRE_PING=true
DB_USE_NULLPOOL=false
DB_POOL_SIZE_RAILWAY=2
DB_MAX_OVERFLOW_RAILWAY=0
```

Remaining live evidence still required:

- Railway `/db_health` output during peak command traffic.
- Real provider availability under the production asset universe.
- MT5/Binance/Bybit sandbox execution proof with broker-side order IDs.
- Outcome coverage recovery proof after the active-signal and expiry fixes are deployed.

External implementation notes checked during this pass:

- TradingView webhooks send alert payloads to user-provided HTTP endpoints, require secure handling, support JSON bodies when the alert message is valid JSON, and cancel requests taking longer than three seconds. SignalRankAI should keep webhook handlers fast, authenticated, and non-blocking.
- MT5 `order_send` requires a structured trade request and broker-side validation of symbol, volume, price, SL, TP, order type, filling type, expiration, and retcode handling. SignalRankAI broker execution should continue to fail with structured reasons before and after broker submission.
- Binance symbol filters such as price, lot size, and notional constraints require pre-trade normalization before order placement.
- Bybit order creation requires category/symbol/side/order type/quantity inputs and exchange-specific validation; execution adapters should normalize broker payloads but preserve provider-specific rejection codes.

## 2026-07-02 follow-up: trading ecosystem intelligence foundation

This pass moves SignalRankAI further away from a one-size-fits-all signal bot and toward a personalized trading ecosystem. The engine now enriches candidate signals with asset registry data, market intelligence, multi-timeframe conflict classification, opportunity scoring, confidence breakdowns, and mission-control health fields before final delivery.

Changes made:

- Added `services/asset_registry.py` for canonical symbols, asset-class classification including indices, provider/broker symbol routes, recommended profiles, and dynamic universe fallback discovery.
- Added `services/market_intelligence.py` to evaluate market open state, session, liquidity, volatility regime, trend regime, news risk, strategy compatibility, asset health, and scan priority.
- Added `services/mtf_consensus.py` so a lower-timeframe SELL inside higher-timeframe BUY context is classified as a counter-trend/pullback setup with a confidence haircut rather than a plain directional signal.
- Added `services/user_intelligence.py` for persistent user preferences: trader style, risk profile, asset classes, preferred/blocked assets, sessions, notification style, execution mode, and broker preferences.
- Added `services/tier_policy.py` to encode Free/Premium/VIP capabilities, delivery delay, TP visibility, asset-class access, auto-trading access, and trade-management access.
- Added `services/opportunity_engine.py` to rank opportunities using technical quality, AI confidence, historical/live performance, market health, R/R realism, time-to-target, and MTF alignment.
- Added `services/mission_control.py` to build live signal mission snapshots with health, TP1 progress, live P/L, probability TP today, recovery probability, risk state, and AI recommendation.
- Added `services/trading_intelligence.py` as the engine-facing adapter for enrichment.
- Wired engine enrichment behind `SIGNAL_INTELLIGENCE_ENGINE_ENABLED`.

## Recommended four-service layout

1. **gateway** — `uvicorn railway_main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`
   Owns health/API, Telegram webhook, commands/callbacks and bot scheduler. Set
   `RUN_ENGINE_LOOP=0` and `RUN_WORKER_LOOP=0`. This is the only public service.
2. **engine** — `python main.py`, `RUN_MODE=engine`,
   `HONOR_RUN_MODE_ON_RAILWAY=true`. Remove its HTTP healthcheck.
3. **worker** — `python main.py`, `RUN_MODE=worker`,
   `HONOR_RUN_MODE_ON_RAILWAY=true`. Owns expiry/maintenance/live outcomes during
   the initial split. Disable ML and shadow ownership here.
4. **analytics** — `python main.py`, `RUN_MODE=analytics`,
   `HONOR_RUN_MODE_ON_RAILWAY=true`. Owns stale/rejected shadow outcomes, bounded
   all-asset candle collection and delayed ML training.

An optional fifth **delivery** service may run the durable receipt reconciler
using `deploy/railway_roles/delivery.env`. It does not replace the engine's
candidate/outbox creation yet, so do not disable the engine delivery-outbox path.

An optional sixth **outcome** service can own live delivered outcomes after
`WORKER_OUTCOME_TRACKER_ENABLED=0` is proven on the worker. Never run both owners.

## AI and Governance

OpenAI is the preferred external intelligence provider. Gemini remains a
compatibility/failover provider, and deterministic local review remains the
final fallback. The AI layer is advisory: it cannot bypass market-data
freshness, stop/target geometry, portfolio exposure, calibration, financial
activation, owner approval, or the global execution kill switch.

Set the OpenAI key as a Railway secret; never paste it into Telegram commands,
logs, tickets, or chat transcripts.

```text
AI_PRIMARY_PROVIDER=openai
AI_PROVIDER_ORDER=openai,gemini,local
OPENAI_API_KEY=<Railway secret>
OPENAI_AI_ENABLED=1
OPENAI_SIGNAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=1
OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-6-luna
OPENAI_SIGNAL_REVIEW_MODEL=gpt-6-luna
OPENAI_DEEP_MODEL=gpt-6-sol
OPENAI_REASONING_EFFORT=low
OPENAI_DEEP_REASONING_EFFORT=medium
OPENAI_SIGNAL_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=5
OPENAI_DEEP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=25
OPENAI_AI_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED=1
OPENAI_AI_WINDOW_SECONDS=60
OPENAI_AI_MAX_CALLS_PER_WINDOW=6
OPENAI_RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS=900
OPENAI_CONFIG_ERROR_COOLDOWN_SECONDS=3600
```

The integration uses the OpenAI Responses API with strict structured output and
`store=false`. Operator commands:

- `/ai`: run the governed aggregate AI review;
- `/ai_review`: inspect the latest provider-routed review;
- `/ai_analyze`, `/ai_audit`, `/ai_predict`: provider-neutral aliases for
  the existing analysis/audit compatibility surfaces;
- `/ai_status`: secret-safe provider/model/budget/circuit diagnostics;
- `/ai_test`: one minimal structured OpenAI connectivity probe.

Gemini fallback:

```text
GEMINI_API_KEY=<optional fallback provider key>

GEMINI_SIGNAL_REVIEW_MODEL=gemini-3.8-flash

```

Legacy Codex/OpenAI aggregate governance variables remain supported where those
older audit paths are still enabled:

```text
OPENAI_CODEX_REVIEW_MODEL=gpt-6-sol

```

# SignalRankAI 1.0.5 Railway Readiness Timeout Hotfix

Railway staging proved that migrations through `0023_signal_runtime_schema`,
PostgreSQL, both Redis roles, Telegram webhook registration, the worker and live
Coinbase REST data were operational. The deployment remained unready because the
database readiness probe allowed only 1.5 seconds while startup maintenance and
Telegram initialization were warming a two-connection Railway pool.

Version 1.0.5 keeps readiness fail-closed while removing the false negative:

- `DB_READINESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` defaults to 8 seconds and is bounded to 2–30.
- readiness uses the reserved `DBPriority.CRITICAL` lane;
- migration head, required runtime columns and the active-thesis unique index
  are checked in one catalogue query instead of four database round trips;
- timeout responses retain a structured reason and the effective timeout.

Recommended Railway value:

```env
DB_READINESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=8
```

## Deployment diagnostics

The pre-deploy command runs the new evidence-first audit:

```bash
python scripts/deployment_diagnostics.py \
  --phase predeploy \
  --strict-core \
  --output /tmp/signalrank_predeploy_diagnostics.json
```

After startup, Railway runs a one-time read-only runtime diagnosis when:

```env
DEPLOYMENT_DIAGNOSTICS_ENABLED=1
```

The report distinguishes:

- `PASS`
- `FAIL`
- `WARN`
- `BLOCKED`
- `SKIPPED`

Missing credentials are never treated as passed tests.

For the full hermetic suite and live provider certification, use an isolated staging certification service:

```bash
python scripts/deployment_diagnostics.py \
  --phase full \
  --run-full-suite \
  --live-providers \
  --continue-on-failure \
  --output /tmp/signalrank_full_diagnostics.json
```

Do not run the deep suite in the customer-facing monolith during normal traffic.

# SignalRankAI 1.0.4 Railway Runtime Schema Hotfix

This release adds Alembic revision `0023_signal_runtime_schema` after Railway
proved that the clean migration chain reached revision 0022 while omitting the
`signals.mfe_pct` and `signals.mae_pct` columns required by the canonical ORM.
The revision is idempotent, preserves data, repairs `performance_version`,
reconciles duplicate active theses, and recreates the partial unique guard.

Readiness and deployment diagnostics now validate the runtime columns and use
PostgreSQL catalog semantics for the partial unique index instead of matching a
fragile textual `pg_indexes.indexdef` representation.

## Scope

This pass moved the latest stabilization work into `SignalRankAI1` and focused on the live Railway symptoms from the July 2 logs:

- PostgreSQL pool exhaustion under monolith scheduler load.
- `/signals` not matching signals actually delivered to the requesting user.
- `/system` being planned but not registered.
- Stock/index/asset discovery diagnostics being too shallow for production triage.
- yfinance connector candles failing freshness checks because they lacked `timestamp`.
- Telegram flood-control retries not being centrally throttled.
- Short-timeframe signals being delivered hours after generation.
- Dashboard win-rate and exposure metrics hiding low outcome coverage.
- SQLAlchemy/asyncpg bind casts failing on raw `:value::jsonb` syntax.

### Stale Signal Delivery Gate

Files:

- `engine/delivery_freshness.py`
- `signalrank_telegram/bot.py`
- `tests/test_delivery_freshness.py`

Added a hard delivery freshness gate so stale opportunities are rejected before Telegram delivery instead of merely showing `Freshness` and `Age` in the message.

The gate now checks:

- signal age by timeframe,
- user trade profile maximum age,
- remaining opportunity decay,
- live price availability,
- current setup validity through the existing stale-signal validator,
- whether TP/SL has already been reached.
- entry drift relative to stop distance,
- current reward/risk after live price movement.

This directly targets the production failure where a `5m` signal could be generated nearly five hours earlier and still be delivered.

The resend pipeline also expires stale candidates before sending, so DB or scheduler recovery should not flush old signals to users.

## Evidence and calculation

Freeze the release SHA, normalized source hash, dependency locks, schema head,
configuration identity, required assets, account policies and acceptance scope.
Use the existing `requirements` traceability and release gates to account for
every merged feature and every master-directive requirement. A requirement is
complete only when its implementation and acceptance evidence are reviewed.
Missing, skipped, mocked-only or stale external evidence remains incomplete.

Before assessment, split each applicable dimension into acceptance criteria
with named owners and equal weights. Each criterion passes only with reviewed
evidence tied to the frozen release; unsupported criteria receive zero credit.
Dimension score = 100 times passed weight divided by applicable weight.
Subsystem score is the mean of its applicable dimensions. Define applicability
before running checks; an unresolved feature cannot be converted to N/A.
Always show failed criteria alongside the score. Do not use averages to hide a
failed security, execution, provider or recovery gate.

Development and feature completeness require all frozen requirements to pass.
Stability 100 means every scoped reliability acceptance criterion passed,
including the actual 24–72-hour soak; it is not an absolute future guarantee.
Enterprise readiness covers the operational, security, governance and support
criteria. Institutional maturity requires every trading lifecycle, account
policy, data provenance, reconciliation and intervention criterion to pass.
The requested percentages cannot authorize execution while any release gate
is blocked, even if an aggregate happens to meet its threshold.

traffic before measurement. A successful health probe is not a latency/load

## New repairs requiring a new immutable candidate

- Explicit failed release evidence overrides an older configured certificate
  ID. Missing engine inventory blocks release, and public-testing configuration
  must pass actual effective database pool limits.
- Load profile hours are converted to seconds. Short or empty runs, HTTP
  throttling/errors, malformed shard counters, inconsistent concurrency and
  nonfinite metrics cannot certify capacity. Long load runs require an explicit
  CLI duration. Seven-day profiles can produce a soak report; passing a
  synthetic report fixture is not an actual soak.
- Generation locks use one canonical scope across engine, Telegram and database
  adapters. Redis Lua atomically checks canonical and historical keys and writes
  a random token with NX and expiry. Redis absence or command failure denies
  acquisition. Release compares the exact token, and task/thread ownership
  prevents inherited child context or a losing contender releasing a winner.
  General cached or asynchronous state writes are not used as lease authority.
- The legacy dedup wrapper imports existing functions, waits for actual async
  checks even inside a running event loop, uses the deduplicator's actual API,
  and cannot report success solely from local memory after lease failure.
- Database errors in legacy active-signal checks block generation.
- SQLAlchemy 2.1 Result, Select and Row annotations use direct column types.
  Nullable Telegram IDs are excluded from Telegram-only queues and broadcasts;
  web-only referrers use canonical user IDs and distinct reward references.
  Legacy performance queries use Signal's actual regime and asset-class
  columns instead of referencing nonexistent Outcome columns.

The new guard decision tests reached 100% line and 95% branch coverage for
`core/release_guard.py`. This is scoped evidence, not an overall core-engine
score. Local database integration includes actual SQL execution for performance
filters, separate web-only referral rewards, idempotent referral replay and
Telegram queue exclusions. The four repaired lock/database modules now join
the zero-error critical typing gate.

The cleanroom verification image includes redis-server and an explicit owned
loopback integration step. The runner clears application credentials, uses a
unique local port and test-key scope, captures tested-source hashes, and stops
its own server. Missing Redis or failed contracts block the step. The default
unit command double is identified separately from actual Redis integration.

## Operating limits and remaining gates

These generation leases are a single Redis instance accelerator. Database
uniqueness and durable delivery/execution idempotency remain necessary across
Redis failover and work exceeding the TTL. A coordinated immutable rollout is
required: historical workers can still write old lock formats. Clustered Redis
with incompatible cross-slot keys denies this script rather than falling back
to local memory. No financial guard is waived by a passing lease test.

Production database storage remained roughly 4.5 GB used of 5 GB. Migration
0046 copies a large legacy table before retiring it, so migration remains
blocked until capacity and restore evidence are adequate. Backup creation is
not restore certification. Temporary Railway SSH registration for downloading
the existing backup awaits explicit owner authorization after automatic
approval review rejected the account-level access change.

Other unresolved gates include dependency vulnerabilities, complete static
analysis, full-runtime typing debt, hosted CI, entitled live provider feeds,
per-tester prop-firm policy verification, actual broker/demo fills and lifecycle
reconciliation, Telegram/web production parity and failure drills, native
device and manual accessibility testing, monitored 24–72-hour soak, and two
complete audits with no new material gaps. Financial activation remains gated.

## Continuation after hosted CI

Draft PR [189](https://github.com/theocriloxr/SignalRankAI/pull/189) published the
recovery as `ae6a6fb4aab968187a4a3aa5e9a8fde807fc33f2`. Its hosted run
`37746622470` passed frontend and research-browser checks. Backend failed
because a test demanded a tilde range instead of accepting the exact Expo 57
pin; the retry additionally loaded persisted trades from an earlier process.
The test now verifies the locked SDK and manifest agree, and tracker unit tests
isolate persistence as well as memory. The failing 106-test batch now passes
locally. This is not yet a new hosted backend certificate.

Static analysis found the new mobile `.npmrc` lacked a minimum release age.
Both Node projects now require a seven-day resolution age, enforce compatible
Node/npm engines, and use npm 11.17.0 in CI. Clean installs, the frontend lint
and production build, mobile type checking, three frontend dependency tests
and all 44 mobile dependency tests passed with this npm version. The npm config
scan passed with zero findings; the full scan passed on 498 files. Frontend's
full dependency audit still reports zero vulnerabilities.

The research continuation repairs actual correlation admission paths:

- Compare percentage returns for identical start/end timestamp intervals,
  rather than raw price levels or unrelated equal-length tails.
- Reject missing, malformed, constant, short, duplicate or unordered histories,
  invalid thresholds and existing-symbol exposure. Never drop invalid rows to
  manufacture sufficient evidence.
- Use the current market-data coroutine in the optional controller gate. The
  old import did not exist, and its exception handler silently admitted signals.
- Require complete shared trade snapshots in the engine and optional controller.
  Redis errors, unavailable shared state and corrupt records cannot become an
  empty portfolio. Existing non-admission callers retain their compatibility
  fallback; the new strict read is explicit.

The focused risk/state/tracker selection passes 179 tests; critical Pyright
reports zero errors and targeted Ruff passes. These checks use synthetic
evidence, not live account or broker certification. Untimestamped correlation
input now blocks admission when exposure exists. Absolute correlation remains
a conservative constraint; it does not establish portfolio netting, account
drawdown, stale-market-data acceptance or per-venue sizing readiness. The
engine's existing synthetic drawdown state is still not real account evidence.
The remaining ordered directives and financial release gates remain open.

## Design, safety and provenance rules

Preserve approved dark/light emerald/silver palette; responsive widths 320 to 1920 CSS px, 200% zoom, reduced motion, forced colors, screen reader and real iOS/Android QA require rendered verification. Use native readable charts; avoid casino-like live tickers and purchased unlicensed effect assets. Unknown currency, balances or broker P&L must not become zero/NGN/USD by assumption.

Broker policy percentage values are decimal fractions: 0.005 means 0.5 percent, not 0.005 percent. Each broker account has its own connection ID and risk policy, with no automatic mirroring or execution. Paper history is simulated; delivery receipts never prove actual fills. Secure demo links never activate trading; freezes disable new execution only.

## Resource pressure contract

`core/resource_governor.py` provides the process-level pressure state machine.
It can sample process RSS, cgroup/host memory limit, process CPU, event-loop lag
and pending asyncio tasks. Runtime owners provide current DB admission depth and
wait, Redis latency, delivery queue depth/capacity, provider error rate and
Telegram `RetryAfter` rate.

States and policy:

| State | New scans | Optional/heavy work | Real execution ceiling | Critical paths |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `OPTIMAL` | allowed | allowed when separately configured | allowed when separately configured | preserved |
| `CONSERVATIVE` | reduced | heavy work paused | allowed when separately configured | preserved |
| `MINIMAL` | reduced further | optional inference and heavy work paused | allowed when separately configured | preserved |
| `CRITICAL` | paused | paused | blocked | health, webhooks, commands, delivery proof, lifecycle, kill switch, payment verification and existing-position tracking preserved |

Escalation is immediate. Recovery requires
`RESOURCE_RECOVERY_SAMPLES` consecutive observations below hysteresis boundaries
and moves down no more than one state at a time. `APP_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB=0` uses a
finite cgroup v2/v1 limit when available and otherwise falls back to host
physical memory. An explicit positive value overrides detection.

The runtime API is:

```python
from core.resource_governor import get_resource_governor

governor = get_resource_governor()
snapshot = await governor.sample(
    db_admission_queue_depth=db_queue_depth,
    db_admission_wait_ms=db_wait_ms,
    redis_latency_ms=redis_latency_ms,
    delivery_queue_depth=delivery_depth,
    delivery_queue_capacity=delivery_capacity,
    provider_error_rate=provider_error_ratio,
    telegram_retry_after_rate=retry_after_ratio,
)
policy = snapshot.policy
```

Every snapshot is JSON-serializable through `snapshot.as_dict()`. The governor
also publishes bounded Prometheus gauges/counters when `prometheus-client` is
installed. A policy is an upper bound only; it never enables a feature that is
disabled by its own configuration or bypasses consent, broker, risk or
kill-switch controls.

# SignalRankAI responsive acceptance

Minimum audit widths: 320,360,375,390,412,430,768,1024,1280,1440,1920 CSS px; 200% zoom and short landscape viewports.

- Desktop: navigation rail and dense two-column signal evidence; table body scrolls within a named, keyboard-focusable region.
- Tablet: disclosure menu and sticky bottom primary navigation only when constrained; no 15-link forced horizontal strip.
- Mobile: touch-friendly 44px targets, 5 high-value destinations, safe-area padded bottom bar, full-width reading order; form inputs must remain readable without horizontal scrolling.
- No financial, signal or broker-critical detail behind hover, canvas or collapsed status.
- Dark/light/system should retain brand integrity, visible focus and readable contrast; `prefers-reduced-motion` disables unnecessary effects.

requirements.text:
# Runtime tooling hardening

The backend root-filesystem scan identified vulnerable vendored code in the
base image's setuptools installation and in both virtual environments' pip
installations. Updating application urllib3/msgpack did not update the copies
inside pip. A credential-free container probe confirmed the embedded
`pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json` manifests and physical vendored module directories.
Those findings were retained as real inventory, without suppressing advisories.

Canonical backend images now keep package installation in their builder stage.
The final filesystem removes pip from both runtime environments and removes
the unused base interpreter's pip, setuptools, wheel and ensurepip. Patched
setuptools/wheel dependencies required by either virtual environment remain.
OS package metadata remains available to the root-filesystem scanner. A clean
final image copies the stripped filesystem and keeps the existing non-root
UID, entrypoint, Python paths, native libraries and application permissions.

`SIGNALRANK_IMMUTABLE_RUNTIME=1` makes `INSTALL_AT_BOOT=true` fail before Python
or the application starts. Changing dependency bytes requires rebuilding and
accepting another image. Development environments retain their explicit boot
installation option when the immutable runtime flag is absent.

Deployment diagnostics use installed distribution metadata and packaging's
requirement/marker rules to check runtime dependency compatibility without an
installer. Missing dependencies, incompatible versions, conflicting installed
versions and malformed dependency metadata fail validation. Diagnostics omit
raw requirement URLs, credentials and exception messages. This check verifies
compatibility; image integrity and vulnerability acceptance are separate gates.

Both dependency environments, native ML/database imports and installed vendor
SDK parser/transport tests run after the Docker runtime stripping step. Actual
deployed root-filesystem scanning and application startup still require fresh
evidence for the new SHA. These changes do not close the outstanding OS or
mobile advisories, broker acceptance, financial activation or full soak gates.

requirements.text:
## Architecture (source contract)
The **browser** uses relative `/api/v1/platform/...` URLs and `credentials: include`. Next.js rewrites this **exact** API prefix to the trusted backend origin from a **server-only** environment variable:

`SIGNALRANK_PLATFORM_API_ORIGIN=https://<trusted-api-host>`

This variable is set **on the Next.js frontend deployment**; it must contain only an HTTPS origin (no path, credentials, query or fragment). For local development only, `http://localhost` and loopback are supported. The browser no longer uses `NEXT_PUBLIC_SIGNALRANK_API_BASE_URL` for sessions.

The backend must keep `APP_COOKIE_SECURE=1`, `APP_COOKIE_DOMAIN` empty for host-only cookies when requests are proxied to the frontend hostname, and cookie path `/`; its existing `SameSite=Lax` session+CSRF cookies then belong to the frontend host. **Do not disable CSRF** and do not set `SameSite=None` merely to bypass an incorrect proxy setup. Ensure the backend's public application base URL points to the frontend for email activation and password links. Keep API and frontend HTTPS throughout.

If the trusted origin is missing, the frontend does **not** silently forward account data to an arbitrary public host. Protected API requests fail with 404 until the setting is supplied. This is an intentional configuration block, not a successful connectivity check.

requirements.text:
# Scanner fairness recovery

The scanner previously truncated the full eligible list to `ENGINE_UNIVERSE_CAP`
before passing it to its persistent queue. Repeated wakeups therefore scanned
the same prefix. Coverage anchors could also replace a popped tail member
without returning that member to pending work.

The scheduler now queues the full observed eligible universe and uses
`ENGINE_UNIVERSE_CAP` only to bound each cycle's work. Rotating class anchors
retain their coverage slots; displaced members return to the front in their
original order. Completed, disabled and already queued members cannot be
reintroduced by this return operation. Runtime class, market-hours, blacklist,
provider, expectancy and risk qualification still apply.

Prospective observations use format 2 and policy `engine-class-round-robin-v2`.
The `scheduled` stage records the full eligible queue input and the policy
explicitly records `universe_cap_scope: per_cycle_work`. Format 1 observations
retain their original prefix semantics, payloads and hashes on restoration.
Historical observations are never relabeled as evidence of the new policy.

Behavioral regressions exercise the actual engine scheduling function: 45
members across five classes with a five-slot work budget, rotating anchors,
disabled members, a budget smaller than the class count, and complete rounds.

## 1. What SignalRankAI is

SignalRankAI is a Telegram-first, multi-asset trading-intelligence platform.
It combines market-data providers, deterministic strategy/risk validation,
optional AI/ML review, Telegram delivery, lifecycle/outcome tracking, paper and
shadow evaluation, tiered product access, Paystack payment readiness, and
Railway deployment/runtime tooling.

It is financial-adjacent software, not a profit guarantee. The system must
never invent a win rate, hide losses, deliver stale data as fresh, or execute
real money without explicit future approval and independent safety controls.

The canonical signal loop is:

```text
market providers
  -> provider health/freshness
  -> strategy generation and confluence
  -> deterministic risk validation

  -> idempotent Telegram delivery
  -> delivery proof + active message ID
  -> user buttons / Check Outcome
  -> outcome lifecycle and notifications
  -> provenance-separated analytics
  -> strategy/provider/automaton recommendations
  -> tier and release diagnostics
```

requirements.text:
## 6. Outcome and performance truth

Outcome events are monotonic and idempotent:

- `TP1`, `TP2`, and `TP3` are separate win events.
- `SL` is a loss event.
- `MISSED_ENTRY` means the entry zone was never reached before expiry.
- `EXPIRED` means the signal expired without resolution.
- `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` is an operational outcome, not a fabricated win/loss.

Performance is separated by provenance: `backtest`, `walk_forward`, `shadow`,
`paper`, `manual`, and `live_delivered`. Reports include sample size, costs,
spread/slippage assumptions, latency, drawdown, expectancy, and methodology.

Evidence thresholds used by the performance layer:

| Sample | Interpretation |
|---:|---|
| `<30` | Exploratory only |
| `30–99` | Early/internal signal |
| `100–299` | Minimum usable internal evidence |
| `300–499` | Stronger promotion evidence |
| `500+` | Candidate for public claims only with disclosed methodology |

Promotion is conservative: adequate sample, multiple positive out-of-sample
folds, positive expectancy, profit-factor/drawdown constraints, and human
approval are required. No code hardcodes or advertises a 60% win rate.

## 7. Automaton and Agent Council

`core.automaton.AutomatonState` supports:

`OBSERVE`, `SIMULATE`, `PAPER_TRADE`, `CONSERVE`, `RECOVER`, `OPTIMIZE`,
`SCALE`, `PAUSE`, and `KILL_SWITCH`.

The default virtual balance is `AUTOMATON_STARTING_BALANCE_USD=5000`; it is not
real money. State decisions consume equity, drawdown, win rate, expectancy,
sample size, provider confidence, delivery latency, DB/Redis/outcome health,
and missed/expired rates. The automaton can recommend lower volume, quarantine,
stricter validation, provider changes, or paper scaling. It cannot trade,
withdraw, fund, deploy, rewrite production, or bypass risk controls.

The Agent Council roles are: Market Data, Strategy Research, Signal Quality,
Risk Manager, Final Delivery Guard, Outcome, Backtest, Shadow Trading, Paper
Trading, Automaton Supervisor, Portfolio, Business, Support, Compliance and
Trust, CodexOps, and Release Guard. Each role has inputs/outputs, forbidden
actions, approvals, fallback, and feature-flag expectations in
`core/agent_council.py`.

## 10. Database and migrations

Postgres is the durable system of record. Redis is used for shared state,
queues, caches, locks, and webhook dispatch where configured. SQLite files in
the repository are local/test artifacts, not the production source of truth.

Migration chain (`db/migrations/versions`):

`0001_init`, `0002_features`, `0003_runtime_state`, `0004_payment_events`,
`0005_bot_events`, `0006_bigint_telegram_ids`, `0007_market_data_cache`,
`0008_user_tier_column`, `0009_archived_column`, `0010_consolidate_full_schema`,
`0011_platform_hardening_security_scaling`, `0012_outcome_notify_state`,
`0013_proxy_nodes`, `0014_add_outcome_pnl_pct`, `0015_active_signal_guard`,
`0016_signal_profile_metadata`, `0017_signal_delivery_proof`,
`0018_signal_lifecycle_events`, `0019_user_timezone_privacy`,
`0020_payment_receipts`.

Run and audit migrations:

```powershell
python -m alembic upgrade head
python scripts/schema_audit.py
```

The current audit reports 20 revisions, one head (`0020_payment_receipts`), and
no revision errors. Never use destructive resets on a live database. Rehearse
the migration on a disposable/staging database first.

### Full-suite exceptions and interpretation

1. `tests/test_web_api_tokens.py::TestWebApiTokens::test_rotate_and_revoke_token`
   expects an unauthenticated token rotation to be `200` or `503`. The secure
   implementation requires an API key and returns `401`, which is the intended
   security contract. The test is legacy/order-sensitive and should be updated

## 14. Release stages

| Stage | Allowed | Disabled until evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Internal owner testing | Manual, paper, shadow, diagnostics, backtests, test receipts | Public payments, auto/copy, real payouts |
| Limited public testing | Bot, profiles, signals, outcomes, paper if stable, support/reporting | Auto/copy, real payouts, paid claims |
| Limited paid beta | Verified Paystack/receipts/refunds/support with disclosed performance | Auto/copy, real payouts, guarantees |
| Public production | Only after clean soak, security review, migration rehearsal, and evidence | Any capability that fails independent safety gates |

`LIMITED_PUBLIC_TEST_READY`, `PAID_BETA_READY`, or
`PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_READY`. The current offline result is limited testing only.

  payments are intentionally not production-enabled.

  establish boundaries before any future physical service split.

10. Only then prepare a controlled production canary and a tiny manual live-money pilot with automatic/copy/prop execution still disabled until separately authorized and certified.
1.2 Completion claims are evidence claims
Status	Allowed meaning
IMPLEMENTED_VERIFIED	Code exists, relevant tests pass, exact-SHA runtime/staging evidence exists, and observed behavior matches the requirement.
IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED	Code exists but exact-SHA test/runtime evidence is incomplete. Must not be counted as done.
PARTIAL	Some code/evidence exists, but important subrequirements remain.
BLOCKED_EXTERNAL	The implementation is ready but an external account/provider/platform action is genuinely unavailable to the agent. State the exact action required.
FAILED	The requirement currently fails and is a release blocker.
DEFERRED	Only allowed for explicitly out-of-scope future features that do not affect current safety, parity, correctness or release readiness.
NOT_APPLICABLE	Must include a rationale and cannot hide a missing requirement.

1.3 Forbidden shortcuts
☐ Do not lower ML/risk/quality thresholds merely to increase signal frequency or satisfy a daily-signal target.
☐ Do not fabricate signals, outcomes, fills, prices, provider health, calibration, win rate or test evidence.
☐ Do not mark a requirement VERIFIED because a runbook, placeholder, wrapper, scaffold or checklist exists.
☐ Do not enable real, automatic, copy, prop or payout execution during certification unless the user explicitly authorizes a controlled pilot after all gates are green.
☐ Do not treat recovery/starvation signals as equivalent to champion-approved live signals. They require a separately labeled cohort and certification.
☐ Do not blend paper, shadow, replay, legacy archive and live-delivery outcomes into one misleading performance number.
☐ Do not let stale, synthetic, ambiguous, ghost-priced or uncertified data become execution-authoritative.
☐ Do not silence security scanners broadly to make CI green. Fix true issues and narrowly justify known false positives.
☐ Do not perform network/provider/ML work while holding database transactions open.
☐ Do not permit a process to report healthy/ready while a required dependency or schema/provenance gate is broken.
☐ Do not reuse certification evidence from an older SHA after any source/config/migration change that affects the release candidate.

2. Current known baseline and evidence boundary
The implementation history has already corrected substantial issues: canonical release manifests, cleanroom certification services, web fan-out ORM materialization, durable event outbox work, database transaction budgets, Telegram queue/handler latency separation, Next.js product shell, API-key secret-boundary hardening, pinned staging identity, static/security cleanrooms, persistent staging PostgreSQL/Redis volumes, and exact-SHA cleanroom passes on earlier candidates. However, the branch has continued to evolve after some of those passes. Therefore, no older cleanroom, staging or production evidence may automatically certify the current branch head.
Known area	Last-known state / directive
Target branch	implementation-of-master-blueprint
Production runtime	Keep existing production isolated from ongoing release-candidate work until staging certification succeeds.
Execution posture	Real/auto/copy/prop execution and real payouts must remain fail-closed during implementation and staging.
Staging topology	Isolated staging project exists with separate frontdoor, engine, delivery, analytics, PostgreSQL and Redis. Persistent volumes were attached to staging PostgreSQL and Redis.
CI/cleanroom	Backend, frontend, mobile and static/security cleanrooms have reached green on prior exact SHAs; re-run on the final current SHA.
Schema	Current intended repository head is 0047_event_outbox or later if further migrations are added. Always compute actual current Alembic head; never hard-code historical 0045/0046 assumptions.
Production Postgres	Previously observed near 90% of a 5-GB volume. Re-check current headroom and expand/retention-plan before production migration/cutover.
Market-data/runtime	Production previously showed stale FX/index/commodity/crypto data and long DB session holds. These require fresh exact-SHA verification after fixes.
ML	Champion/challenger was correctly fail-closed in prior evidence; drift and limited forward live-delivery evidence remained. Re-certify by segment.
Web frontend	Default Next.js starter was replaced, but full feature parity, route-specific live data, auth flows and E2E must be certified.
GitHub protection	Historically main/staging protection was not enabled. Re-check and enforce rulesets/required checks externally if not controllable from the connected tool.

IMPORTANT: The AI must begin by re-reading the current exact branch head and runtime. This document is a requirements and audit directive, not a substitute for current evidence.

3. P0 signal integrity, lifecycle, paper-trading and outcome defects
The Telegram messages supplied on 01 October 2026 expose several state-integrity failures that must be treated as P0 because they can make a signal appear profitable, active, stale, expired or missed using mutually inconsistent facts. These must be reproduced in tests and fixed before any live-trading verdict can be YES.
ID	Problem	Required resolution
P0-SIG-001	US30 canonical price mutation / lifecycle inconsistency	Original VIP signal shows entry 50,686.17 and stop 50,877.72. Later TP1 notification for the same signal ID shows entry 51,321.24 and stop 51,484.80. A single signal ID must never silently mutate canonical entry/SL/TP values. Separate observed market price from planned levels and preserve immutable signal-plan fields.
P0-SIG-002	Immediate “signal stale” paper rejection followed by entry trigger	US30 paper trade was rejected as stale at 15:15, then the same signal became entry-triggered at 15:16. Staleness, actionability, entry-trigger logic and paper-open logic are racing or using different clocks/evidence. One canonical actionability evaluator must gate both.
P0-SIG-003	TP1 false/contradictory evidence	JNJ SHORT has entry 262.2601 and TP1 260.8439, but the TP1 alert at 20:02 states current price 262.45 and +0.54%. For a short, 262.45 is above entry and far above TP1. Outcome tracking must never declare a TP from incompatible price evidence.
P0-SIG-004	Missed-entry signal assigned -3.69R	BAC expired with “Entry Not Triggered” yet the outcome reports -3.69R. If the entry never triggered, trading R/P&L must be N/A/0 according to an explicit missed-entry accounting policy, not a losing trade.
P0-SIG-005	Duplicate terminal notifications	US30 “Signal Expired” was sent more than once after prior activity/TP/risk-free updates. Terminal-state transitions and notifications require idempotency keys and a single legal terminal transition.
P0-SIG-006	Paper trades repeatedly not opening	US30 rejected as stale; JNJ/BAC rejected for profile preference mismatch; BAC rejection duplicated. Verify owner/user paper settings, matching rules, default profile behavior, signal eligibility and notification idempotency so eligible delivered signals automatically open exactly once when paper auto-open is enabled.
P0-SIG-007	Delivered signal missing from /signals	JNJ was delivered and entry-triggered, but /signals displayed US30 only. Later BAC appeared while JNJ remained omitted. Delivered/active list must be derived from canonical delivery + lifecycle state, not an inconsistent cache or paper eligibility state.
P0-SIG-008	Engine pulse accounting gap	Pulse reports 5 decision rows, 3 accounted, 2 unaccounted. Every decision row must terminate in an auditable generated/delivered/rejected/deferred/failed reason. Unaccounted must be zero or a release alert.
P0-SIG-009	Recovery-signal semantics	US30/JNJ/BAC were explicitly “PAPER ONLY — serving-model recovery signal” while raw model scores were below the certified 84% cutoff. Recovery signals must remain a separate cohort, owner/paper/demo-only by default, with separate outcome statistics and never contaminate champion performance.
P0-SIG-010	Expiry vs active/risk-free state	US30 became active and reached a risk-free update, then later expired as “setup no longer actionable.” Define whether an active triggered trade can expire; usually expiry applies only before entry. After entry, lifecycle should move through ACTIVE/TP/SL/CLOSED, not pre-entry EXPIRED.

3.1 Required canonical signal state machine
Implement or verify one authoritative state machine, with database constraints or transition guards, that all Telegram, web, paper, outcome and broker flows consume. Suggested states may be adapted, but illegal transitions must be impossible.
Phase	Legal examples	Forbidden examples
Candidate	SCANNED → STRICT_CANDIDATE → ML_REJECTED / RISK_REJECTED / APPROVED	Rejected candidate becoming delivered without a new decision event.
Approved/pre-entry	APPROVED → DELIVERED → WAITING_ENTRY → ENTRY_TRIGGERED or EXPIRED/MISSED_ENTRY	EXPIRED then ENTRY_TRIGGERED; mutable canonical entry/SL/TP.
Triggered	ENTRY_TRIGGERED → ACTIVE → TP1/TP2/TP3/SL/BE/CLOSED	ACTIVE → pre-entry EXPIRED; TP hit without price crossing target in direction.
Paper execution	ELIGIBLE → PAPER_OPEN_PENDING → PAPER_OPENED → PAPER_CLOSED or PAPER_REJECTED(reason)	Duplicate opens; “profile mismatch” without explaining which preference mismatched.
Broker execution	ELIGIBLE → ORDER_SUBMITTING → ACKNOWLEDGED → FILLED/PARTIAL/REJECTED → RECONCILED	Assuming fill because API request returned 200; no reconciliation receipt.
Terminal	MISSED_ENTRY, PREENTRY_EXPIRED, SL, BE, TP1_PARTIAL, TP2_PARTIAL, TP3/CLOSED, MANUAL_CLOSE, CANCELLED	Multiple incompatible terminal outcomes for same canonical lifecycle version.

3.2 Canonical immutable plan vs observations
☐ Persist immutable plan version: signal_id, plan_version, asset identity, side, timeframe, strategy, created_at, entry zone/trigger rule, stop, targets, risk assumptions, expiry rule, provider lineage and release/model IDs.
☐ Persist observations separately: observed price, provider, observed_at, event type, confidence/freshness, raw payload hash.
☐ Every lifecycle transition stores evidence IDs and the exact observation that caused the transition.
☐ Notifications render from the canonical plan + the transition observation; they must never recompute entry/stop/targets from a new price snapshot.
☐ If a plan is amended, create a new version with an explicit amendment event; never mutate history silently.
☐ Outcome R uses actual triggered entry/fill basis according to policy; missed entries have no trade P&L.
☐ All clocks use UTC internally; WAT/localized times are display-only. Expiry comparisons use one canonical server time source.
3.3 Paper trading acceptance policy
☐ Create a paper eligibility decision object with explicit fields: enabled, account/profile, asset class allowed, symbols allowed/denied, timeframe allowed, recovery-signal policy, max open positions, risk budget, stale/actionable result, duplicate result and final reason code.
☐ Default owner demo profile should not silently reject equities/indices if the product claims multi-asset paper support. If a preference intentionally rejects a signal, Telegram/web must show exactly which setting caused it and provide a one-click route to change it.
☐ Auto-open only after entry trigger if that is the product policy; otherwise clearly distinguish “queued paper intent” from an opened paper position.
☐ Use a unique key such as (paper_account_id, signal_id, plan_version) to guarantee exactly-once opening.
☐ Duplicate “Paper Trade Not Opened” messages are prohibited; notification event idempotency is required.
☐ Paper fills must use realistic spread/slippage/lot-step/tick-size/market-session rules per asset class. Do not assume crypto-style sizing for US30/JNJ/BAC.
☐ Paper ledger, position ledger and outcome ledger must reconcile after restart and be reconstructible from durable events.

requirements.text:
4. Decision accounting, delivery parity and recipient truth
4.1 Zero unaccounted decisions
☐ Every engine decision row receives a terminal decision_status and reason_code.
☐ Engine pulse “Accounted” must equal evaluated decisions; “Unaccounted” must be zero in normal operation.
☐ If a decision is interrupted by process crash, a recovery worker must finalize it as deferred/failed with an explicit reason, then retry if safe.
☐ Build an invariant check and alert: evaluated = generated + all rejection buckets + deferred + failed.
☐ Expose funnel counts by asset class, timeframe, strategy, provider, regime and model cohort.
☐ Ensure “generated in latest cycle” and “generated in trailing hour” use clearly labeled windows so the pulse cannot look contradictory.
4.2 One delivery truth across Telegram and web
☐ Telegram and web must read the same canonical delivered-signal set and lifecycle status.
☐ /signals and web /app/signals must include all confirmed recipient deliveries that remain active/actionable according to lifecycle, regardless of paper-open preference.
☐ Delivery eligibility and paper eligibility are separate decisions. A paper preference mismatch must not hide a delivered signal.
☐ Every channel stores receipt_id, channel, user, signal_id, sent_at, confirmed_at if available, latency, failure reason, retry count and terminal delivery status.
☐ Web fan-out must continue materializing ORM data inside active sessions and must have a real PostgreSQL regression test for detached/expired rows.
☐ Delivery retry is idempotent; dead-letter queues are observable; duplicate user-facing messages are prevented by notification idempotency keys.
☐ Reconcile Telegram delivery counts, web notification counts, recipient entitlements and /signals list membership continuously.
4.3 Notification lifecycle correctness
☐ Notification templates are generated only after state transition commit or via a transactional outbox tied to that commit.
☐ Risk-free/breakeven messages require a valid active position and a price path that actually reached the configured threshold.
☐ TP alerts require target crossing or fill evidence appropriate to the asset and side; never infer TP from unrelated current/stored values.
☐ Expired/missed-entry notifications cannot fire after entry-triggered/active unless there is a distinct “order intent expired before fill” state.
☐ Terminal notifications are exactly-once per user/channel/event version.
☐ All replies/references resolve to full signal IDs, not ambiguous shortened IDs.

requirements.current_implementation: Original source retained in full. Clause-level implementation and acceptance are not established by this index.
requirements.verification_method: Review every retained clause against active call paths, then attach behavioral evidence to its ID.
requirements.text:
5. Market data, instrument identity and provider certification
The system has correctly rejected stale data in prior production observations; preserve that fail-closed behavior. The goal is not to make stale warnings disappear by weakening limits, but to make certified fresh feeds available for each enabled asset class.
5.1 Provider matrix by asset class
Asset class	Execution-authoritative requirements	Fallback policy
Crypto	Certified exchange/aggregator OHLCV + quote, symbol/venue identity, clock/freshness, tick/lot metadata.	Fallback may support research only unless independently certified for execution-sensitive decisions.
FX	Broker-grade or certified FX feed with session/calendar, quote freshness, spreads and symbol mapping.	Do not rely on Yahoo/yfinance as execution-authoritative primary feed.
Indices	Broker/provider feed matching the actual index/CFD instrument identity and session.	Legacy Yahoo may be analysis-only if explicitly labeled and never used for entries/execution.
Equities	Exchange/market-data source with market hours, corporate actions, splits and symbol metadata.	Delayed data must be labeled and blocked from time-sensitive signal execution.
Commodities	Certified underlying/CFD/futures source with contract identity, session and roll logic.	Do not mix spot/futures/CFD prices under one symbol without explicit normalization.

5.2 Mandatory data-quality gates
☐ Freshness thresholds by timeframe and provider capability; source timestamp and receive timestamp both recorded.
☐ Ghost-price / plausible-range checks by instrument using dynamic reference bands rather than brittle hard-coded values.
☐ OHLC consistency: low <= open/close <= high; nonzero/valid price; monotonic timestamps; expected interval continuity.
☐ Cross-provider sanity for execution-sensitive quotes when practical; record disagreement and fail closed beyond tolerance.
☐ Symbol alias registry with canonical instrument ID. Eliminate synthetic leakage such as malformed symbols that produce zero data.
☐ Market calendar/session gate: stocks, indices, futures/commodities only trade when the selected instrument/venue is actually open or the strategy explicitly supports extended hours.
☐ Provider health is capability-specific. “Provider healthy” for crypto does not prove it is healthy for indices/commodities.
☐ Provider certification artifacts must include tested symbols, timeframes, timestamps, freshness distribution, missing-candle rate, error rate, latency, fallback use and exact release SHA.
5.3 Class-fair opportunity scheduling
☐ Preserve persistent round-robin/interleaving across open asset classes, not a crypto-first list truncated by cycle caps.
☐ Guarantee each enabled/open asset class receives bounded scan opportunities even under a large crypto universe.
☐ Weight by market-open state, data-provider health, user demand, historical opportunity density and compute budget without starving low-count classes.
☐ Expose per-class attempted/scanned/qualified/delivered counts and maximum scan age.
☐ Add invariant/alert when an enabled open class receives no scan within its SLO.

clauses.text: 5. Market data, instrument identity and provider certification

The system has correctly rejected stale data in prior production observations; preserve that fail-closed behavior. The goal is not to make stale warnings disappear by weakening limits, but to make certified fresh feeds available for each enabled asset class.
Asset class	Execution-authoritative requirements	Fallback policy

Crypto	Certified exchange/aggregator OHLCV + quote, symbol/venue identity, clock/freshness, tick/lot metadata.	Fallback may support research only unless independently certified for execution-sensitive decisions.
FX	Broker-grade or certified FX feed with session/calendar, quote freshness, spreads and symbol mapping.	Do not rely on Yahoo/yfinance as execution-authoritative primary feed.
Indices	Broker/provider feed matching the actual index/CFD instrument identity and session.	Legacy Yahoo may be analysis-only if explicitly labeled and never used for entries/execution.
Equities	Exchange/market-data source with market hours, corporate actions, splits and symbol metadata.	Delayed data must be labeled and blocked from time-sensitive signal execution.
Commodities	Certified underlying/CFD/futures source with contract identity, session and roll logic.	Do not mix spot/futures/CFD prices under one symbol without explicit normalization.
☐ Freshness thresholds by timeframe and provider capability; source timestamp and receive timestamp both recorded.
☐ Ghost-price / plausible-range checks by instrument using dynamic reference bands rather than brittle hard-coded values.
☐ OHLC consistency: low <= open/close <= high; nonzero/valid price; monotonic timestamps; expected interval continuity.
☐ Cross-provider sanity for execution-sensitive quotes when practical; record disagreement and fail closed beyond tolerance.
☐ Symbol alias registry with canonical instrument ID. Eliminate synthetic leakage such as malformed symbols that produce zero data.
☐ Market calendar/session gate: stocks, indices, futures/commodities only trade when the selected instrument/venue is actually open or the strategy explicitly supports extended hours.
☐ Provider health is capability-specific. “Provider healthy” for crypto does not prove it is healthy for indices/commodities.
☐ Provider certification artifacts must include tested symbols, timeframes, timestamps, freshness distribution, missing-candle rate, error rate, latency, fallback use and exact release SHA.
☐ Preserve persistent round-robin/interleaving across open asset classes, not a crypto-first list truncated by cycle caps.
☐ Guarantee each enabled/open asset class receives bounded scan opportunities even under a large crypto universe.
☐ Weight by market-open state, data-provider health, user demand, historical opportunity density and compute budget without starving low-count classes.
☐ Expose per-class attempted/scanned/qualified/delivered counts and maximum scan age.
☐ Add invariant/alert when an enabled open class receives no scan within its SLO.

6. ML, calibration, learning and recovery signals
6.1 Preserve fail-closed champion/challenger governance
☐ Candidate models must never auto-promote solely because they trained successfully.
☐ Promotion requires non-inferiority or defined improvement across discrimination, calibration, expectancy and risk metrics on chronological/purged forward-style validation.
☐ Feature schema hash and training-serving parity are mandatory.
☐ Model registry must record data window, features, label policy, code SHA, model artifact hash, calibration method, threshold, metrics and authorization.
☐ Schema-version migration requires explicit authorization and compatibility proof.
☐ If drift is detected but candidate regresses, keep champion and enter monitor/research mode rather than weakening criteria.
6.2 Segmented validation
☐ Report calibration, pass rate, win/loss/partial/missed-entry, expected R, drawdown and coverage by asset class × strategy × timeframe × regime × provider cohort.
☐ Do not infer broad multi-asset readiness from a few hundred mixed live-delivery rows.
☐ Use chronological/purged walk-forward validation where overlapping labels/time horizons could leak future information.
☐ Monitor ECE/Brier/reliability plots, PR-AUC/ROC-AUC where appropriate, positive precision/recall and coverage. A high precision at extremely low recall must be interpreted with signal frequency and evidence size.
☐ Separate market regime drift from provider/data-pipeline drift and feature-engineering drift.
6.3 Recovery/starvation cohort
☐ Recovery/starvation signals are a separate model_policy_cohort with explicit reason, champion raw score, challenger score if any, certified threshold and recovery threshold.
☐ By default deliver recovery signals only to owner/admin paper/demo/advisory surfaces, never public live execution.
☐ Calculate recovery-cohort outcomes separately from champion-approved outcomes.
☐ Do not label a recovery signal “high-conviction” solely from a composite heuristic when the certified model score is well below threshold. UI must explain that it is an experimental recovery observation.
☐ Require a minimum forward sample, calibration/expectancy evidence and explicit promotion decision before recovery logic can influence live-money execution.
6.4 Learning from outcomes
☐ Outcome labels must be lifecycle-correct; missed-entry and no-trade examples are not losing fills.
☐ TP/SL labels must be supported by canonical price-path evidence and ordered event timestamps.
☐ Shadow rejects require enough post-decision market data to determine counterfactual outcome without look-ahead leakage.
☐ Archive/replay/shadow examples receive lower or separate weighting from true forward delivered outcomes.
☐ Learning jobs cannot run network or heavy ML operations inside DB sessions; use short reads/writes and bounded queues.
☐ No model training result may overwrite champion artifacts without atomic registry update and rollback capability.

7. Paper trading, portfolio accounting and performance truth
7.1 Transactional paper ledger
☐ All cash, reserved margin, positions, fills, fees, realized/unrealized P&L and adjustments are durable SQL ledger entries.
☐ No in-memory-only financial state is authoritative.
☐ Ledger entries are append-only/immutable where appropriate and idempotent under retries.
☐ Paper order open/close is transactionally reconciled with position state and signal lifecycle.
☐ Restart/replay reconstructs the same account balances and positions.
☐ Concurrency tests cover duplicate opens, simultaneous exits, partial targets and process crashes.
7.2 Asset-specific sizing
☐ Risk sizing uses account equity × configured risk percentage divided by monetary loss per unit at stop, not a generic “units” formula.
☐ For FX use contract size/pip value/quote conversion; for indices use point value/contract specs; for equities use share granularity; for crypto use step/min-notional; for commodities use contract/tick specs.
☐ Enforce provider/broker lot step, minimum, maximum and margin constraints.
☐ Paper UI and Telegram make clear whether a displayed size is shares, lots, contracts, units or notional.
☐ If instrument metadata is missing, do not suggest a precise live size; return “cannot size safely” with reason.
7.3 Performance reporting
☐ Separate forward delivered, paper executed, shadow, replay/backtest and legacy archive performance.
☐ Do not count missed entries as executed wins/losses.
☐ Show sample size, confidence interval/uncertainty, expectancy, average R, profit factor, max drawdown, win/loss/BE/partial/missed-entry rates and coverage.
☐ Outcome coverage must approach 100% for eligible delivered signals; unresolved/stale outcomes are an SLO.
☐ Performance must be reproducible from canonical ledgers and outcome events.

8. Broker/demo/live execution architecture
8.1 Broker connection and demo certification
☐ Broker credentials are encrypted/secret-managed, never logged, never stored in Telegram chat, and withdrawal permissions are unnecessary/prohibited.
☐ Connection wizard validates account type, currency, leverage where relevant, server/venue, symbol mapping, quote access and trading permissions.
☐ Demo certification must test: authenticate, account snapshot, symbol lookup, quote, contract metadata, market/limit order if supported, SL/TP, partial close, full close, cancel, reconnect, duplicate request/idempotency and reconciliation receipts.
☐ Every broker request has client_order_id/idempotency key and immutable request/response audit metadata excluding secrets.
☐ Order acknowledgement is not fill. Reconcile actual broker order/fill/position state after timeout/restart.
☐ If broker/API state is ambiguous, freeze further execution for that order/account and reconcile before new risk is added.
8.2 Live eligibility gates
☐ Exact release SHA certified and provenance endpoint matches deployed SHA/image/schema.
☐ Provider feed certified for that exact instrument/asset class and currently fresh.
☐ Broker demo certification current for the same adapter/account capability set.
☐ Global and account-level kill switches functional and drill-tested.
☐ Portfolio daily-loss, max-open-risk, per-symbol, per-class, correlation/concentration and news/session limits configured.
☐ No unresolved delivery/outcome/reconciliation queue backlog.
☐ No active critical security, DB, provider, model-drift or stale-data incident.
☐ User explicitly enables a controlled pilot after reviewing limits; automatic/copy/prop features remain separately gated.
8.3 Controlled live pilot
☐ Start with tiny manual-money exposure and one broker/account; do not jump directly to prop capital.
☐ Keep auto execution off initially. Use SignalRank as decision support and manually verify broker quote, spread, market session, news, entry, SL and TP.
☐ Exclude recovery signals from initial live pilot.
☐ Set hard daily loss, max concurrent risk, max order count and max notional/contract limits that cannot be bypassed by UI.
☐ Require canary period and explicit post-trade reconciliation. Any mismatch pauses the pilot automatically.
☐ Advance automation only after separate forward evidence and execution-reconciliation evidence.

9. Database, event durability and concurrency
9.1 Database session SLO
☐ No provider network call, broker call, AI/LLM call, sleep, heavy feature computation or long loop while an SQLAlchemy session/transaction is open.
☐ Adaptive candle persistence is batch-buffered and wall-clock bounded; dropped/deferred noncritical evidence is visible and replayable where required.
☐ Critical decision/signal/financial writes use short prioritized transactions with explicit timeouts.
☐ Observe session-hold duration by label and priority; alert on p95/p99 and critical holds beyond target.
☐ Analytics/training workloads are isolated from trading-critical DB pools/roles where practical.
☐ Use proper indexes, query plans and retention/partitioning for large decision, candle, event and outcome tables.
9.2 Production storage headroom
☐ Re-check production PostgreSQL volume utilization before any migration or increased telemetry rollout.
☐ Expand production storage if headroom is below policy; recommended alert thresholds 60/75/85% with action runbooks.
☐ Report per-table/index growth and retention policy for candles, decisions, rejected/shadow events, logs and delivery/outcome evidence.
☐ Vacuum/analyze/bloat monitoring must be operational.
☐ Backup retention and restore capacity must account for the expanded schema/data volume.
9.3 Durable event/outbox
☐ Critical events use Redis-first plus PostgreSQL transactional outbox fallback or an equivalently durable design.
☐ Outbox insert is tied to the authoritative DB transition where possible; no gap between state commit and event persistence.
☐ Claim uses short transactions / SKIP LOCKED; network publish happens after claim transaction.
☐ Retry uses bounded backoff, attempt counters, dead-letter state and metrics.
☐ After Redis recovery, worker replays exactly once semantically using idempotency/inbox protection.
☐ Health/readiness must not report healthy merely because an in-memory fallback exists.

10. Telegram, web, mobile and product parity
10.1 Telegram
☐ Webhook HTTP acknowledgement must be fast and separate from async queue delay and handler duration SLOs.
☐ Commands are idempotent and do not block the webhook on network/DB-heavy work.
☐ /signals, /signal, paper controls, watchlists, alerts, settings and account actions resolve to canonical platform APIs/state.
☐ /apikey never creates or reveals a persistent secret in chat. Telegram may show metadata and direct the user to authenticated web settings.
☐ Reply buttons and callbacks carry stable IDs and reject stale/ambiguous actions safely.
☐ Duplicate lifecycle/paper rejection messages are prevented.
10.2 Web product
☐ Complete public routes: home, pricing, methodology, risk, security, status, docs and providers with production content, accessibility and responsive design.
☐ Complete authenticated routes: overview, signals, signal detail/evidence, markets, research, watchlists, alerts, notifications, paper, portfolio, performance, journal, brokers, billing, referrals, support, settings, developer/API, and owner operations.
☐ No production hard-coded localhost API base. Same-origin or environment-configured API only.
☐ Authentication, session expiry, MFA/recent-auth for sensitive actions, API-key one-time reveal, device/session management and logout are complete.
☐ Signal detail visually distinguishes plan, observations, model cohort, delivery receipts, paper state, lifecycle transitions and outcome evidence.
☐ Owner operations shows provider health, queue depth/age, DB saturation, model/drift state, release SHA/schema, dead letters, backup status and execution switches.
☐ Use Playwright E2E and axe accessibility tests for critical flows and mobile breakpoints.
10.3 Mobile
☐ Native Android/iOS build/type/security gates pass from lockfile.
☐ Mobile consumes canonical API contracts rather than duplicating business logic.
☐ Critical UX supports signal viewing, alerts, watchlists, paper state, broker status and account/security workflows as intended by product scope.
☐ Push notification tokens, deep links and auth/session lifecycle are secure and idempotent.
☐ No web-export requirement unless the project intentionally supports Expo web; Next.js remains the primary web client.

11. Security, authentication and secrets
11.1 Security gates
☐ Ruff, critical Pyright, Bandit, pip-audit, Semgrep and ShellCheck are hard release gates with explicit severity policy.
☐ Semgrep scans runtime code comprehensively; migrations are covered by migration/schema certification. Narrow false-positive exclusions only.
☐ Frontend/mobile npm audit gates block high/critical vulnerabilities unless an explicit reviewed exception exists.
☐ Generate SBOM and image/dependency provenance for the release artifact.
☐ Runtime image is minimal, non-root, multi-stage; compilers/git/build tools remain builder-only unless runtime truly needs them.
☐ Container/image scan must be added if available and high/critical findings resolved before production.
11.2 Auth/session controls
☐ Password/session/MFA flows are rate-limited and auditable.
☐ Sensitive operations (API key creation, broker credential changes, execution enablement, payouts, MFA changes) require recent authentication and MFA when configured.
☐ Session inactivity/absolute expiry and revocation are enforced server-side.
☐ CSRF/session-cookie/security headers/CORS are correctly configured for the deployment model.
☐ No secret values or secret-source aliases appear in logs, diagnostics, error messages, analytics or client bundles.
☐ API keys are hashed at rest, scoped, expiring, revocable, last-used tracked; raw secret shown only once in authenticated web flow.
☐ Broker secrets and API keys are never entered through or echoed by Telegram.
11.3 Config alias safety
☐ Canonical environment variables have documented aliases, precedence and deprecation timeline.
☐ True boolean aliases with contradictory values fail closed in staging/production.
☐ Separate safety layers (e.g., AUTO_EXECUTION_ENABLED vs AUTO_TRADE_ENABLED) are not misclassified as aliases; validate dependency invariants instead.
☐ Secret aliases may coexist for rotation but must not be logged/compared in a way that leaks values.
☐ Emit a sanitized configuration fingerprint with no secrets to prove deployed roles share the intended release profile.

12. CI, release manifest, Docker, provenance and branch governance
12.1 One executable source of release truth
☐ certification/release_manifest.yaml (or successor) is the canonical gate registry.
☐ GitHub CI, cleanroom Docker, staging certification and production release tooling consume that manifest rather than re-declaring divergent commands.
☐ Every required command exists and runs. Missing scripts in a manifest are a failing gate, not documentation debt.
☐ Release manifest validates unique gate IDs, environments, commands and manual-gate semantics.
☐ Python 3.11 production-lock path is canonical; Python 3.12 compatibility may be tested but does not replace the production dependency lock unless intentionally promoted.
12.2 Exact-SHA evidence
☐ Each evidence artifact names git SHA, branch, build/deployment ID, schema head, model version, environment/project identity and timestamp.
☐ /version exposes immutable release provenance without secrets.
☐ /healthz is process liveness only; /readyz validates bounded critical dependencies and returns 503 if not ready.
☐ Railway expected branch/SHA gates block wrong-source deployments.
☐ Any source change after certification requires a new SHA and new certification/soak.
12.3 Branch protection
☐ Protect main and staging/release branches with required PR review/checks and prevent direct force pushes/deletions.
☐ Require the canonical CI/cleanroom checks for merges to main.
☐ Ensure production services source the canonical release branch/immutable image, not an old fix branch.
☐ Do not repoint production until staging exact-SHA certification is complete.
12.4 Repository hygiene
☐ Remove/archive stale generated artifacts such as old Ruff reports after fresh exact-SHA scans prove current status.
☐ Classify TODO/FIXME/placeholders as active requirement, intentional future work, legacy/dead code or test fixture; no ambiguous TODO remains in active runtime.
☐ Archive obsolete fix documents and old release instructions into a historical evidence area so operators cannot follow stale steps accidentally.
☐ Keep historical migrations/evidence intact; do not rewrite history to make current tests pass.
☐ Reduce giant monolithic modules into domain services where it materially improves testability, ownership, startup isolation and failure containment. Thin wrappers alone do not satisfy decomposition.

☐ Any source change after certification requires a new SHA and new certification/soak.
☐ Protect main and staging/release branches with required PR review/checks and prevent direct force pushes/deletions.
☐ Require the canonical CI/cleanroom checks for merges to main.
☐ Ensure production services source the canonical release branch/immutable image, not an old fix branch.
☐ Do not repoint production until staging exact-SHA certification is complete.
☐ Remove/archive stale generated artifacts such as old Ruff reports after fresh exact-SHA scans prove current status.
☐ Classify TODO/FIXME/placeholders as active requirement, intentional future work, legacy/dead code or test fixture; no ambiguous TODO remains in active runtime.
☐ Archive obsolete fix documents and old release instructions into a historical evidence area so operators cannot follow stale steps accidentally.
☐ Keep historical migrations/evidence intact; do not rewrite history to make current tests pass.

☐ Reduce giant monolithic modules into domain services where it materially improves testability, ownership, startup isolation and failure containment. Thin wrappers alone do not satisfy decomposition.

13. Staging, migration, backup/restore and failure injection
13.1 Isolated staging requirements
☐ Separate Railway project/environment identity from production, with separate PostgreSQL, Redis, Telegram/test bot or safe channel, broker demo credentials and payment test mode.
☐ Persistent volumes attached and verified by actual disk usage/restart persistence.
☐ Pinned staging identity cannot be spoofed by copying environment overrides into production; exact project ID/profile/override controls must agree.
☐ All live-money execution/payout variables hard-off in staging. Global kill switch on.
☐ Frontdoor/migration owner runs guarded migration first; other roles boot only after schema gate passes.
☐ Every role verifies exact expected SHA, schema head and environment profile.
13.2 Migration and restore
☐ Alembic has one head and complete offline-render chain.
☐ Run upgrade from representative previous production schema to current head on staging copy/fixture.
☐ Validate decision log, event outbox, paper ledger and critical constraints/indexes after migration.
☐ Perform backup/restore drill on exact release schema and prove restored application boots/reads/writes safely.
☐ Production migration requires verified backup evidence and rollback/forward-repair plan.
☐ Never run production backup policy against isolated staging simply because Railway’s default environment label says “production”; canonical pinned identity decides semantics.
13.3 Failure injection
☐ Restart each role during active queues; verify no duplicated deliveries, paper opens or lifecycle transitions.
☐ Kill Redis; prove critical events persist to DB outbox and replay after recovery.
☐ Introduce DB saturation/lock contention; critical decisions should remain bounded and noncritical candle/analytics writes should yield/defer safely.
☐ Feed stale/ghost/malformed provider data; verify no tradable signal can pass.
☐ Simulate broker timeout/ambiguous acknowledgement; prove reconciliation and duplicate-order protection.
☐ Send duplicate Telegram webhook/payment events; prove idempotency.
☐ Crash between state transition and notification; prove transactional outbox recovers without losing or duplicating the event.
☐ Corrupt/mismatch expected SHA/schema/environment; readiness/release gates must block startup/cutover.
